# Splunk Modular Input Exporter

Exports logs, metrics, and traces as newline-delimited Splunk HEC JSON events to standard output.

Each output line is one complete Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC) event.
This is useful when a parent process, such as a Splunk modular input, collects
standard output and forwards the events for indexing. It is included in the
Splunk-specific component set through `internal/components.Get()`.

All settings are optional. The default configuration is `splunk_modinput: {}`.

<!-- config autogenerated section -->
## Configuration
| Setting | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| ------- | ---- | ------- | -------- | ----------- |
| `index` | string |  | no | Default destination index. An empty value lets the output consumer select its default index. |
| `source` | string |  | no | Default HEC source identifying the event origin. |
| `sourcetype` | string |  | no | Default HEC sourcetype identifying the event format. |
<!-- end config autogenerated section -->

Telemetry attributes override configured defaults. Logs use resource attributes
followed by log record attributes. Metrics and traces use resource attributes.
The corresponding attributes are `com.splunk.source`, `com.splunk.sourcetype`, and
`com.splunk.index`. Translation follows the upstream
[Splunk translator](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/pkg/translator/splunk).

```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: localhost:4317

exporters:
  splunk_modinput:
    source: my-application
    sourcetype: otel
    index: main

service:
  pipelines:
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [splunk_modinput]
    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [splunk_modinput]
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [splunk_modinput]
```

## Behavior and limitations

The exporter writes synchronously and serializes writes across its instances and
signals. It leaves standard output open on shutdown. Collector diagnostic logs
should use standard error so they do not mix with HEC events.

The exporter uses Collector exporter helpers for standard internal telemetry.
It does not buffer, queue, or retry writes, since retrying a partially written
request can duplicate events. Errors propagate to the caller; a request may
already have written some events when it fails. Writes to a blocked standard
output can block the pipeline; context cancellation is checked between events,
but cannot interrupt an operating system write already in progress.

The exporter performs no authentication or index authorization. Configure these
at the input boundary. The Splunk OTLP input applies its HEC token index
restrictions before forwarding data to this exporter.

The HEC representation can lose OpenTelemetry-specific information. Histogram
and summary metrics can expand into multiple events; unsupported metric types
follow the translator's behavior. This exporter does not produce OTLP JSON.

## Development

From this directory, run `go generate -tags mdatagen ./...` to refresh component metadata and
standard config, lifecycle, and goroutine leak checks. Run `go test -race ./...`
for tests and `go test -run '^$' -bench . -benchmem` for signal benchmarks.

This component is hosted outside OpenTelemetry contrib. A future donation still
requires the upstream proposal, sponsor, code owners, and review described in the
[donation requirements](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/main/docs/new-components.md).
